items.heading: Look At the Numbers Once,
items.text: Look at the numbers once, calmly, because they explain why planning only around one exam is risky.

items.heading: These Lanes Are Ordered
items.text: These lanes are ordered by realistic growth headroom, meaning how far income and independence can stretch with skill and proof, not by prestige or exam difficulty. That is a judgement, not a rule.

visuals.heading: Ask for the Approval, Not

items.heading: Ask for the Approval, Not
items.text: Ask for the approval, not the brochure. The regulator or council approval, the attached hospital or lab details and the last three years of results tell you more than any advertisement.

items.heading: Do the Total
items.text: Do the total-cost sum for every year. Add tuition, hostel, exam and clinical fees for the whole course, then compare against a realistic first salary. If the gap is large, look at a lower-cost lane first.

items.heading: Keep One Backup Running
items.text: Keep one backup running in parallel. A backup lane is not a lack of faith. It protects the year if the main plan misses.

items.heading: Let the Student Describe
items.text: Let the student describe the daily work. If your child can explain what a nurse, a lab scientist or a data analyst actually does in a day, the choice is real. If not, arrange one conversation with a working person first.
